confidence_interval_method.why: Wilson remains well behaved at small denominators and at proportions of exactly zero or one, unlike the normal approximation.

instability_findings.rule: flagged unstable when denominator < 30 or Wilson 95% interval width > 0.25

metadata_label_consistency.interpretation: Metadata is descriptive and is NOT treated as ground truth. Mixed-label sources are surfaced for review only; no example is relabeled by this audit.
hypotheses_not_resolved: High-confidence false positives may reflect label noise in the source (the label is wrong and the model is right).
The same pattern may reflect a genuine model bias toward over-flagging that source's benign style (the model is wrong).
These two hypotheses are not distinguishable from aggregate counts alone; resolving either would require human review of the affected rows and would still not be an automatic relabel.

signal_availability.conclusion: Source and category are offline dataset diagnostics. They are not present on the deployed inference request, so no source-based allowlist, blocklist, or routing rule can be enforced at inference time without changing the request contract and establishing a trustworthy client-supplied source value.

deployed_decision_rule.note: This audit changes no decision rule and implements no allowlist. It only characterises what each gateway behaviour would do with the same measured outcomes.

interpretation: Fail-open minimises false blocking of benign prompts but lets every abstained malicious prompt through, raising false negatives.
Fail-closed minimises missed malicious prompts but blocks every abstained benign prompt, raising false positives.
Human review sits between the two and costs review capacity; the review figures here assume a perfect reviewer and are an optimistic upper bound.
The choice between these behaviours is a product risk decision about relative cost, not something validation data can decide.
